headline: OpenAI bans China-linked ChatGPT accounts that amplified US data center electricity price backlash
summary: Two clusters used AI-generated content to stoke fears over US data center energy costs and spread anti-tariff propaganda, though they generated little authentic engagement.
details: OpenAI has banned two clusters of ChatGPT accounts believed to be operating from China, which used its models for covert influence campaigns targeting U.S. tech and policy debates. One group, "Data Center Bandwagon," created social media comments and comic strips blaming AI data centers for rising household electricity bills.

These accounts, operated via VPNs, posed on X as Americans and prompted ChatGPT in Simplified Chinese. A second cluster, "Tech and Tariffs," generated anti-tariff cartoons and spread false claims that ChatGPT user data had been stolen.

OpenAI assessed that the "Data Center Bandwagon" operators were likely a social media team at a private Chinese tech company working for provincial-level government clients. They specifically asked ChatGPT for comic strips about a grid operator's capacity auction prices, posting the output on X.

The concern over data center power costs is a real, documented dispute; PJM Interconnection's market monitor has blamed data centers for a 75.5% increase in power costs in the largest U.S. grid region. Three U.S. senators have demanded answers from Amazon, Google, and Meta over these costs.

The "Tech and Tariffs" cluster focused on U.S.-China competition around tariffs, rare earths, and AI, generating content in English, Italian, Japanese, and Traditional Chinese. One operator described the accounts as a "water army," a Chinese term for coordinated troll networks.

OpenAI's full threat report found that the activity generated virtually no authentic engagement, rating it Category One on the Breakout Scale. The campaigns followed China's 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations, which elevated AI as a strategic industry.

headline: iOS 27 lets you create your own custom iPhone wallpapers, moving beyond stock options
summary: Apple's upcoming iOS 27 update introduces a highly anticipated feature, allowing users to design and apply personalized wallpapers directly on their iPhones. This marks a significant step in device customization.
details: Apple's latest iOS 27 update brings a significant enhancement to iPhone personalization: the ability for users to create their own custom wallpapers. This new feature allows for greater creative freedom beyond the standard collection of pre-set backgrounds.

Previously, users were limited to Apple's curated selections or static images from their photo library. With iOS 27, the system will offer tools or prompts to generate unique designs, potentially leveraging AI or user input for dynamic results.

This development is expected to be a popular addition, giving iPhone owners more control over the look and feel of their devices. It aligns with a broader trend of increased customization options across mobile operating systems.
